wineries.name: Stone Tower Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Hilltop estate with panoramic Blue Ridge views and a serious wine program.
wineries.editorial: Stone Tower sits on Hogback Mountain at the western edge of Loudoun. Two sides to the property: the polished Tower View Tasting Room (21+ club) and the casual, all-ages Harvest Barn. Both share the view that justifies the drive.
policyNotes: Outside food NOT permitted — both tasting rooms have food menus
Leashed dogs welcome inside and outside Harvest Barn; outside Tower View only
Harvest Barn: family-friendly, all ages, walk-in (no reservations for groups of 8 or fewer)
Max 2.5-hour visit per party in public spaces
Closed Tuesday and Wednesday

wineries.name: Bluemont Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 951 feet up — arguably the best view in Virginia wine country.
wineries.editorial: Bluemont's elevation is its whole pitch and it delivers. The patio looks east over the Loudoun Valley toward DC on a clear day. Bring a sweater in any season; the wind up here has opinions.
policyNotes: Outside food and beverage explicitly prohibited — Virginia ABC regulations cited
No outside alcohol
Dogs welcome: inside tasting room + panoramic terrace; leashed required
Food available on site: boards, flatbread, brunch weekends
Live music Saturdays ~3:30–6:30 PM (Sunset Saturdays); occasional Friday member events
Credit card required for reservations; $10/person no-show fee
Family-friendly including dogs ('four-legged friends')

wineries.name: Breaux Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Sprawling Cajun-influenced estate, the most-awarded vineyard in Virginia.
wineries.editorial: Breaux is big — over 100 acres planted — and the experience matches the scale. Stretch out on the lawn, order the muffuletta from the kitchen, and work through the Nebbiolo or the Viognier.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome leashed outdoors (EXCEPT Orleans Patio); also inside Vin 97 tasting room
Outside food permitted outdoors only; NOT inside tasting room
Groups 8+ must use picnic grounds, not patio
No outside alcohol of any kind — Breaux wine only
Kitchen open daily 11 AM–5 PM; gourmet light fare and freshly baked bread
Guided tastings require reservation; only 2 per day accepted

wineries.name: Lost Mountain Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Appointment-only Bordeaux-style cellar (formerly RdV) — widely regarded as Virginia's best producer.
wineries.editorial: Lost Mountain Vineyards is the new chapter of what was RdV Vineyards — same hillside in Delaplane, same Bordeaux-style ambition, new name. A proper appointment: book a ~90-minute experience, taste through the flagship blends, leave understanding why people compare Virginia to Bordeaux on its best days.
policyNotes: Rebranded from RdV Vineyards in 2026 — same property, new name
By appointment ONLY — no walk-ins; reservations via Tock
Tasting Experience runs ~1.5 hours
Hillside vineyard with Blue Ridge views
Bordeaux-style blends; small boutique production

wineries.name: Barboursville Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Italian-owned estate surrounding Jefferson-designed ruins. Iconic.
wineries.editorial: The Zonin family bought this property in 1976 and have been making serious Bordeaux and Italian varietals here ever since. Walk the ruins of Governor Barbour's Jefferson-designed mansion, eat at Palladio restaurant, taste through the Octagon.
policyNotes: No outside food in tasting room — seasonal charcuterie/cheese available on site
Dogs leashed in main tasting room ONLY — NOT in Library tasting room or inside buildings generally
Palladio Restaurant on site: fine dining; lunch Wed–Sun, dinner Fri–Sat (reservation required)
Library 1821 tastings: reservations recommended
Historic estate: ruins of 1814 Barboursville Mansion on grounds

wineries.name: King Family Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Polo matches Sunday afternoons, world-class Meritage all year.
wineries.editorial: King Family hits every note of the modern Virginia winery: serious wine program (the Meritage is the flagship), gorgeous outdoor lawn, food trucks on weekends, and Sunday polo matches in season.
policyNotes: BYO food welcome; no outside alcohol
Dogs welcome leashed outdoors
Shop: local cheeses, charcuterie, baguettes, crackers, preserves, nuts
Polo Sundays: Memorial Day weekend through mid-October (weather/field permitting)

wineries.name: Veritas Vineyard & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Blue Ridge backdrop and a full kitchen for sit-down lunch with the wine.
wineries.editorial: Veritas is dialed in — the wines are good, the views are great, and the Terrace serves real lunch (sandwiches, salads, charcuterie) until 4:30pm. The Farmhouse next door is a B&B if you want to make it a weekend.
policyNotes: BYO picnic permitted in Bricks outdoor area; order wine at bar
Dogs welcome leashed on lawn and veranda; NOT inside tasting room
Food menu on site: shareable items indoors and outdoors
Live music: Starry Nights Summer Music Series + special events throughout year

wineries.name: Early Mountain Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Steve Case's flagship — sophisticated wood-fired food, focused tastings.
wineries.editorial: Early Mountain is the most thoughtfully designed tasting room in Virginia. The food matches the wine, the seasonal Meadow is enormous, and the tasting flights are well-curated for someone trying to understand Virginia for the first time.
policyNotes: Outside food NOT permitted — licensed as a restaurant
No outside alcohol
Dogs welcome leashed outdoors; water bowls and treats provided
Thu–Mon only; closed Tue–Wed; weekend hours vary for private events
Subtly kid-friendly — families welcome

wineries.name: Pearmund Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: One of Virginia's oldest Chardonnay vineyards, walk-in friendly.
wineries.editorial: Pearmund is unfussy. The vineyard's older Chardonnay vines produce one of the best whites in the state. The main winery is adults-only; families head to the Pearmund Farmstore next door.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome on leash outdoors; cleanup required
Food platters available: meats, cheeses, nuts, dips, chocolates
Daily 10 AM–6 PM; Fridays until 8 PM
Main winery is 21+ only; Farmstore location is family-friendly

wineries.name: Greenhill Winery & Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Middleburg estate. Adults-only, sparkling-strong, all-day Mezze menu.
wineries.editorial: Greenhill is the rare Virginia winery that pulls off elegant without being stuffy. The Blanc de Blancs is the bottle to know. The Mezze menu (cheeses, charcuterie, caviar) plays nicely with whatever you're drinking. Strict 21+ throughout — leave the kids and infants at home.
policyNotes: 21+ ONLY
Dogs welcome in outdoor areas; leash required
No outside food inside tasting room (outdoor BYO policy not explicitly stated — verify)
On-site Mezze Menu: cheeses, charcuterie, bread, caviar; self-serve accoutrement bar
Groups 10+ require advance reservation

wineries.name: Chrysalis Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Norton specialists — America's native grape, taken seriously.
wineries.editorial: Chrysalis planted the largest Norton vineyard in the world here. If you've never tried Virginia's native grape, this is the place to start. The onsite Little River Bakehouse serves pizza, paninis, and salads alongside the wine.
policyNotes: Outside food and beverages NOT permitted
Dogs leashed in outdoor areas ONLY — commercial kitchen and cheese creamery require VDACS animal exclusion indoors
Food on site: pizza (Little River Bakehouse), Locksley Farmstead artisan cheese, crackers, dips, spreads
Last food/beverage call 30 min before close
Closed New Year's Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas; 5 PM close Dec 24 and 31

wineries.name: Ingleside Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Tidewater estate, fourth-generation family, picnic-perfect courtyard.
wineries.editorial: Ingleside is a drive from DC but worth the day. The Tidewater terroir produces wines unlike anywhere else in Virginia. The European-style courtyard with the fountain is the picnic spot of the trip.
policyNotes: Pets welcome in European-style courtyard
BYO picnic welcome in courtyard
Gourmet cheeses and sausages available for purchase
Summer Music Series: live music on patio during summer

wineries.name: Scribe Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Mission Revival hacienda on a Sonoma hilltop — long lunches and slow afternoons.
wineries.editorial: Scribe is the Sonoma winery that turned 'family-style lunch with the wine' into a national story. Reservations far in advance. Bring people you want to spend three hours with.
policyNotes: Estate visits require Scribe Viticultural Society (SVS) membership; membership currently open
Dogs welcome in outdoor areas
Book via Tock (members) or reservation form (Knoll Picnic)
Families with young children welcomed by staff

wineries.name: Ridge Vineyards — Lytton Springs
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Old-vine Zinfandel specialists. The honest tasting room in Healdsburg.
wineries.editorial: Ridge is what serious wine people send their friends to in Sonoma. The Geyserville and Lytton Springs blends are the bottles to know. Patio with vineyard views, no pretension.
policyNotes: 21+ only; no children or infants
Reservations recommended; by appointment

Salumi board add-on available ($50)

wineries.name: Domaine Serene
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Dundee Hills Pinot Noir flagship — hilltop estate, focused tastings.
wineries.editorial: Domaine Serene is the Pinot Noir address in the Willamette Valley. The Clubhouse sits at the top of the Dundee Hills with views across the valley to Mount Hood on a clear day.
policyNotes: Outside food and beverages NOT permitted onsite
Dogs welcome leashed on patio
Food on site: bread, oysters, charcuterie, cheese, chips, sliders

wineries.name: Linden Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A quiet, terroir-obsessed mountainside winery for serious wine drinkers who want to think and not perform.
wineries.editorial: Linden is the rare Virginia winery that treats tasting as an intellectual exercise — vintages and vineyard sites compared side by side, with founder Jim Law's fingerprints on every pour. The view is gorgeous, but the policies (no kids, no pets, no groups over four) make it clear this is a place to slow down rather than party. Bring your own picnic to enjoy on the deck after you taste, and you'll see why the wine cognoscenti consider this the soul of Virginia wine.
policyNotes: Adults only (21+) — no guests under 21 including infants
Pets NOT permitted

wineries.name: Glen Manor Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A working Blue Ridge mountainside vineyard with serious Bordeaux-style reds and one of the best views in Virginia.
wineries.editorial: Tucked against Shenandoah National Park, Glen Manor is a small family operation where Jeff White grows everything he bottles on punishing mountain slopes — and the wines (especially the Hodder Hill blend) prove it. You don't get food here, so pack a real picnic; leashed dogs are welcome outside, kids are fine, and the view down the valley is the kind that makes you forget you have a 4pm reservation somewhere else. Walk-ins are accommodated for parties of four or fewer; anything bigger needs to call ahead.

wineries.name: The Winery at La Grange
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An 18th-century manor-house winery just outside DC where weekend afternoons mean live music, picnics, and Virginia reds.
wineries.editorial: La Grange has a restored stone manor at its center, picnic tables on the lawn, and weekend live music that turns it into the closest thing to a true wine-country day trip from the DC suburbs. They sell cheese, hummus, baguettes, and spreads to enhance your visit, but they also actively welcome you to bring your own picnic — a real rarity. Dogs on leashes are good outside; service dogs only inside the manor.

wineries.name: Boxwood Estate Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A polished, French-inspired estate where Middleburg horse country meets Bordeaux-style blends served from a chic stone courtyard.
wineries.editorial: Boxwood is 100% estate, hyper-focused on Bordeaux varieties, and the experience matches — a beautiful tasting room, a Chai (French cellar), and a courtyard with fire tables under a giant river birch. It's strictly 21+, no pets, no outside food beyond a birthday cake, which keeps the vibe more wine-bar-in-the-vineyard than picnic-blanket-Saturday. Reserve a table for weekends; walk-ins are welcome but the space is intimate.

wineries.name: Michael Shaps Wineworks
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A no-nonsense Charlottesville winery from a Burgundy-trained vet pouring both his Virginia wines and imported Maison Shaps Burgundies.
wineries.editorial: Michael Shaps is the closest you'll get in Virginia to a proper Burgundy domaine — he literally makes wine in both places. The tasting room is relaxed and dog-friendly, with a big deck, stone patio, and front lawn where picnicking is encouraged; cheese and baguettes are sold inside if you didn't bring your own. Open daily, walk-ins welcome, and a quieter alternative to the busier C'ville-area names.
policyNotes: BYO food permitted outdoors — picnicking on lawn/patio encouraged
Dogs welcome leashed outdoors; must clean up
Cheese and charcuterie plates available; food trucks on select days
Walk-ins welcome — no reservations required

wineries.name: Iron Horse Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The sparkling-wine icon of Sonoma — outdoor tastings at the end of a long winding road with views that almost outshine the bubbles.
wineries.editorial: Iron Horse has been pouring sparkling wine at the White House since 1985, and the tasting room — really, a glorified outdoor pavilion with a vintage redwood barn behind it — sits at the top of Green Valley with maybe the best view in Sonoma. Book ahead (especially weekends), bring a picnic if you reserve the picnic area, and plan on spending two hours over a glass of Russian Cuvée. Kids are allowed; dogs are not.
policyNotes: Reservations required; book 2+ weeks ahead for weekends
No pets — service animals with documentation only (emotional support animals excluded)

wineries.name: Three Sticks Wines
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An 1842 adobe right off Sonoma's town square, restored by Ken Fulk, serving cult Pinot and Chardonnay in pure historical-glam style.
wineries.editorial: Three Sticks tastes you inside the Vallejo-Castañada Adobe — a sumptuously restored 1842 building one block from Sonoma's plaza. The design is theatrical (Ken Fulk did it), the wines are serious Sonoma Pinot and Chardonnay from estate vineyards like Durell and Gap's Crown, and the experience is decidedly grown-up: no kids, no dogs, max six guests per party. Book ahead — there are no walk-ins.

21+ strictly — no guests under 21, no infants, no dogs
Adobe historic property: refined tranquility focus

wineries.name: MacRostie Winery & Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A glass-walled Estate House on Westside Road delivering panoramic Russian River Valley views and elegant Pinot and Chardonnay.
wineries.editorial: MacRostie's Estate House is a modern glass pavilion that looks straight down the Russian River Valley, with terraces wrapping the building so every seat has a view. The wines (single-vineyard Pinot and Chardonnay) are top-tier, but it's the hospitality — leashed dogs welcome on the patio, live music on 'Serene Sundays,' caviar add-ons if you want to push the boat out — that puts it on every Healdsburg shortlist. Book on Tock; walk-ins aren't really a thing.

wineries.name: Gary Farrell Vineyards & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A hilltop temple to Russian River Pinot and Chardonnay with forested treetop views and serious, seated tastings.
wineries.editorial: Gary Farrell perches on a wooded ridge above Westside Road, and the tasting rooms — multiple intimate patios under the trees — feel more like a private home than a winery. The focus is laser-tight on single-vineyard Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, and the experience matches: seated, guided, 21+, no pets, by reservation only. It's not a casual stop, but if you care about Russian River Valley wine, it's essential.

21+ only including infants — no exceptions

wineries.name: Frog's Leap Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An organic, solar-powered, totally unpretentious Rutherford farm where you taste on the porch of a 1880s yellow farmhouse.
wineries.editorial: Frog's Leap is the antidote to Napa's polish — a working organic farm with a red barn, gardens, and a Vineyard House porch that's set up for long, relaxed seated tastings. The wines (Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Rutherford Cab) are honest and beautifully made, the staff treats you like a friend, and they're one of the few Napa wineries that actually allow dogs on certain outdoor experiences. Note: no picnics on the property per county rules.

wineries.name: Cakebread Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A second-generation Napa stalwart known for Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, and one of the valley's most thoughtful food-and-wine programs.
wineries.editorial: Cakebread is the rare big-name Napa winery that's stayed truly family-run, and it shows in the tasting experience: warm, communal, and food-forward (the on-site culinary program is part of why they're famous). They offer a daily Family Tasting that welcomes kids — uncommon in Napa — and outside food is firmly not allowed per county rules. Reserve well ahead; this is one of the most-visited tasting rooms in the valley.

wineries.name: Castello di Amorosa
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An authentically built 13th-century-style Tuscan castle in Napa — moats, drawbridge, dungeon and all — with surprisingly good Italian-style wines.
wineries.editorial: Castello is the Disney-Napa hybrid you didn't know you wanted: a fully realized medieval castle with 107 rooms, frescoed great hall, and yes, a torture chamber. The tour is the point, and tickets include grape juice for kids ($25 general admission for under-21s). Wines lean Italian — Sangiovese, Barbera, Cab — and well-behaved leashed dogs are welcome on outdoor portions of the tour. Reserve ahead, wear walking shoes, leave the stroller in the car.

wineries.name: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The Cabernet house that beat Bordeaux in 1976 — still pouring CASK 23, S.L.V., and FAY against the Stags Leap Palisades.
wineries.editorial: This is the Cab that won the Judgment of Paris, and the estate has the gravity to match: a modern visitor center looking up at the dramatic Stags Leap Palisades, with the legendary S.L.V. and FAY vineyards visible from your seat. The Estate Experience descends into the wine caves; the Signature is a more standard seated tasting on the patio. Strictly 21+, no pets, no walk-ins — this is a reverent, grown-up visit.

wineries.name: Far Niente
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A 19th-century stone winery, vintage car collection, lavish gardens, and Oakville Cab — Napa's most cinematic estate.
wineries.editorial: Far Niente translates as 'without a care,' which is the goal — a beautifully restored 1885 stone winery, manicured gardens, a museum of vintage Italian cars, and Chardonnay and Cabernet served in the Great Hall. The tour goes through the historic caves before a seated tasting. Strictly by appointment, 21+ only, no dogs, no kids, and book at least two weeks ahead. This is bucket-list Napa.

21+ only; no children

Food included in tasting: seasonal chef-inspired cheese plate with wine flight

wineries.name: Hermann J. Wiemer Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The Finger Lakes' definitive Riesling house — biodynamic, low-intervention, set in a converted 90-year-old barn on Seneca Lake.
wineries.editorial: Wiemer is the name critics like Eric Asimov reach for when they argue American Riesling can stand with Germany. The tasting room is inside a beautifully restored scissor-trussed barn on the west shore of Seneca Lake, the wines are seated and à la carte (design your own flight), and they're explicit about welcoming leashed pets and family members alike. Reservations recommended; walk-ins welcome.

Reservations highly recommended; walk-ins if space allows
Limos and buses not permitted on property
Small-production artisan Finger Lakes estate winery

wineries.name: Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The pioneer that proved vinifera could survive Finger Lakes winters — multi-generational, with sparkling, Riesling, and Keuka Lake views.
wineries.editorial: Dr. Frank is the historical heart of Finger Lakes wine — Konstantin Frank planted the first European vinifera here in the 1960s and his descendants now run a charming, multi-format hospitality program on a Keuka Lake bluff. The Signature Seated Tasting is the structured option; Eugenia's Garden is a walk-up outdoor wine bar where you can sit with a flight, a glass, or a cheeseboard. Dogs are welcome in the outdoor garden but not the tasting room.

wineries.name: Lamoreaux Landing Wine Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An elegant Greek Revival-inspired tasting room on the Seneca Lake bluff, picnic tables out back, top-tier estate Riesling within.
wineries.editorial: Lamoreaux Landing's clean-lined, columned tasting room sits high above Seneca Lake's east shore, and the back lawn is dotted with picnic tables that have what locals consider one of the best lake views in the region. They explicitly welcome picnics on the lawn (no outside food in the tasting room itself), leashed dogs are fine inside and out, and the wines — especially the Riesling and Gruner — punch well above the $12 tasting fee.

wineries.name: Ravines Wine Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A European-trained winemaker plus chef wife running one of the Finger Lakes' most polished tasting rooms inside a historic barn.
wineries.editorial: Ravines is run by Morten Hallgren (trained in France) and his chef wife Lisa, and their Geneva flagship reflects both: Old World dry Rieslings and Cab Francs in a beam-and-slate barn, plus a serious in-house restaurant — the Ravinous Kitchen — doing wine-friendly small plates. The lawn is broad enough that families and leashed dogs both fit comfortably. Reservations encouraged but walk-ins generally work.

wineries.name: Stoller Family Estate
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Dundee Hills sustainability poster child — net-zero tasting room, vast lawn, tire swing in the vineyard, and Pinot for days.
wineries.editorial: Stoller is the rare wine experience that genuinely welcomes everyone — kids run free on the lawn, leashed dogs are welcome on the patio, and the panoramic Dundee Hills view from the LEED Gold-certified tasting room never gets old. The wines (Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, rosé) are solid, the food menu enhances them, and they actively encourage you to bring your own picnic. One of the most relaxed and family-friendly stops in Oregon wine country.

wineries.name: King Estate Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The largest biodynamic vineyard in North America — a hilltop château with sweeping views and Oregon's flagship Pinot Gris.
wineries.editorial: King Estate sits on a hilltop south of Eugene with the kind of European-style château architecture you don't expect in southern Willamette. It's North America's largest certified biodynamic vineyard, the Pinot Gris is what built their reputation, and the tasting room has views over the valley that feel like Tuscany. The on-site restaurant scaled back to a tasting-room food menu in 2023, but you can still pair flights with serious bites.

wineries.vibeDescriptor: Dundee Hills pioneer (since 1971) with a lawn full of sling chairs, Pinot in the glass, and Friday-night 'Live on the Lawn' summer concerts.
wineries.editorial: Sokol Blosser planted some of Oregon's first Pinot vines in 1971 and now hands the winery off to the second generation, who've made it both serious and fun. The hillside lawn is dotted with sling-back chairs around fire pits, the tasting room is sleek and walk-in friendly, and their Live on the Lawn summer concert series (Fridays) is the kind of low-key wine country evening Instagram dreams of. Outside food isn't allowed — they sell their own.

wineries.name: Ponzi Vineyards
wineries.address: 19500 SW Mountain Home Road, Sherwood, OR 97140
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A founding Oregon Pinot family (since 1970) in a modern hilltop tasting room with bocce courts and Chehalem Mountain views.
wineries.editorial: The Ponzi family helped invent Oregon Pinot Noir, and their Sherwood tasting room — a glass-walled hilltop building with bocce courts and a covered terrace — is the polished version of their pioneer story. Tastings run a structured 90 minutes for $50; the wines (Laurelwood District Pinot in particular) are top-tier. Children are welcome if supervised, and reservations are strongly encouraged though walk-ins fit in when space allows.

wineries.name: Becker Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Texas Hill Country institution — a German-stone barn winery surrounded by lavender fields and one of the most-awarded names in the state.
wineries.editorial: Becker has been Texas Hill Country wine royalty since 1992, sitting on a property that includes a reconstructed 19th-century German stone barn, lavender fields in bloom from May, and a Pavilion event space. The tasting room is large and walk-in friendly, picnics are explicitly welcome on the grounds (no outside alcohol), and leashed dogs are fine outside. Worth the drive between Fredericksburg and Stonewall.

wineries.name: William Chris Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 100% Texas-grown, fiercely terroir-focused — the cult name in Hill Country reds, served at a historic 1905 Hye farmhouse.
wineries.editorial: William Chris is the winery most insiders point to when they argue Texas can make wine that competes with anywhere. Everything is 100% Texas fruit, the focus is Tempranillo, Mourvedre, and Cab Franc, and the tasting happens in and around a restored 1905 farmhouse with a sprawling lawn. Tastings are scheduled (11am, 1:30pm, 4pm with variation by day), it's 21+, leashed dogs are welcome outside, and they'll pre-make you a $20 picnic lunch with 24 hours notice — or you can bring your own.

policyNotes: Reservations recommended. Walk-ins welcome when possible, but many days including Saturdays and holidays are fully booked.
Well-behaved dogs welcome on patios. Only service dogs allowed inside. Mention your dog when making reservations.

wineries.name: Peju Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A genuinely welcoming, family-owned estate with stunning grounds featuring art, architecture, fountains, and marble sculptures...
wineries.editorial: A genuinely welcoming, family-owned estate with stunning grounds featuring art, architecture, fountains, and marble sculptures. The lush gardens and soaring ceilings of the remodeled tasting room create a captivating, artistic atmosphere. Known for warm hospitality and making every guest feel at home.
policyNotes: Reservations encouraged but walk-ins welcome when space allows. Book online through Tock.
Dog-friendly winery. Families and friendly pups welcome.

wineries.name: Artesa Vineyards & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A stunning hilltop winery with breathtaking panoramic views of Carneros vineyards, San Pablo Bay, and...
wineries.editorial: A stunning hilltop winery with breathtaking panoramic views of Carneros vineyards, San Pablo Bay, and San Francisco skyline. Award-winning modern architecture built into the hillside with elegant Spanish decor. The spacious terrace offers unmatched views with fountains and photo-worthy landscapes. Sophisticated yet inviting.
policyNotes: Reservations highly recommended, especially on weekends. Book at least a couple weeks in advance for weekend visits.
Dogs allowed on patio and wine tasting lounge. Not allowed on winery tours. Service dogs permitted everywhere.

wineries.name: Robert Mondavi Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An iconic Napa Valley institution celebrating the pioneering vision of Robert Mondavi.
wineries.editorial: An iconic Napa Valley institution celebrating the pioneering vision of Robert Mondavi. Features immersive tours, educational tastings, and curated culinary pairings. The recently transformed estate offers spacious patios with vineyard views. A must-visit for wine history enthusiasts, though experiences can feel more commercial.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended at least one week in advance. Walk-ins and day-of reservations offered based on availability.
Service dogs welcome outside only at main estate. Must be kept on leash.

wineries.name: Opus One
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The pinnacle of luxury wine tasting in Napa Valley.
wineries.editorial: The pinnacle of luxury wine tasting in Napa Valley. This joint venture between Mondavi and Rothschild offers an exclusive, refined experience with stunning architecture and valley vistas. Jazz music accompanies tastings of current vintage and library selections. The Partners' Room offers breathtaking views surrounded by beautiful art. Elegant, prestigious, and memorable.
policyNotes: Appointment only. Reservations available up to two months in advance, released on the first of each month. Online limited to 4 guests; contact directly for up to 8 guests.
Pets not permitted anywhere on the estate. Only ADA-defined service animals allowed.

wineries.name: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A legendary winery famous for winning the 1976 Judgment of Paris.
wineries.editorial: A legendary winery famous for winning the 1976 Judgment of Paris. The FAY Outlook & Visitor Center features luxury interiors and expansive outdoor overlooks with stunning panoramic views of FAY Vineyard and the Stags Leap Palisades. Cave tours and artisanal food pairings elevate the experience. Refined, historic, and prestigious.
policyNotes: Reservations required. Book via email (reservations@SLWC.com), phone, or website.
Only certified service animals allowed. Pets cannot be accommodated.

wineries.name: Inglenook
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A storied 1879 estate owned by Francis Ford Coppola, featuring 1,700 acres with 235 organically...
wineries.editorial: A storied 1879 estate owned by Francis Ford Coppola, featuring 1,700 acres with 235 organically certified vineyard acres. The grand chateau atmosphere includes the elegant Pennino Salon with chandeliers and a European-inspired al fresco bistro courtyard. Rich in history with wonderful atmosphere and impeccable hospitality. Cinematic and romantic.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended well in advance. Contact: 707-968-1179 or reservations@inglenook.com
Dogs not allowed in interior spaces. Welcome on outdoor terrace with wines.

wineries.name: Domaine Carneros
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An elegant French-style chateau situated atop a knoll with sweeping vineyard views.
wineries.editorial: An elegant French-style chateau situated atop a knoll with sweeping vineyard views. Features a grand staircase, formal gardens, marble-floored fireside salon, and expansive outdoor terraces. Specializes in sparkling wines with Taittinger heritage. Seated tastings led by experienced wine professionals create an elevated, classy experience perfect for special occasions.
policyNotes: Reservations required for all 21+ visitors. Book online or call 800-716-BRUT.
Only service animals permitted. Pets not allowed.

wineries.name: Castello di Amorosa
wineries.address: 4045 St. Helena Highway North, Calistoga, CA 94515
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A truly unique experience - an authentically constructed 13th-century Tuscan castle with 107 rooms, a...
wineries.editorial: A truly unique experience - an authentically constructed 13th-century Tuscan castle with 107 rooms, a medieval torture chamber, armory, and grand barrel room. Family-friendly with self-guided and guided tour options. The castle grounds feature resident animals. A fantasy-like, immersive experience that feels like stepping back in time to medieval Italy.
policyNotes: Reservations required for everyone to enter. General admission available without reservation for groups under 15.
Dogs welcome on grounds and self-guided tours. Not allowed on guided tours. May have restrictions in tasting room/gift shop.

wineries.name: Sterling Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Famous for its aerial gondola ride to a hilltop winery with stunning valley views.
wineries.editorial: Famous for its aerial gondola ride to a hilltop winery with stunning valley views. The Greek-inspired white architecture perched atop a 300-foot hill offers a unique arrival experience. Self-guided tastings allow you to explore at your own pace while enjoying panoramic Napa Valley vistas. Fun, scenic, and memorable for the gondola experience alone.
policyNotes: Reservations required for wine tastings. Book online seven days a week.
Pets not permitted on property. Service animals welcome.

wineries.name: Cakebread Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A family-owned winery known for consistently stellar wines and a warm, inviting atmosphere.
wineries.editorial: A family-owned winery known for consistently stellar wines and a warm, inviting atmosphere. The vibrant courtyard has an easy, open-air feel perfect for lingering over each pour. Tours through the working winery provide educational insights while seasonal food pairings showcase culinary excellence. Refined yet approachable hospitality.
policyNotes: Appointment only. Reservations confirmed with full payment. Cancellations 48 hours in advance fully refundable.
Pets not permitted inside per health regulations. Wine Club Members may bring one pet to outdoor Wine Club Lounge.

wineries.name: Schramsberg Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A historic sparkling wine producer with fascinating underground caves dating to the 1800s.
wineries.editorial: A historic sparkling wine producer with fascinating underground caves dating to the 1800s. Famous for being served at White House state dinners. Cave tours wind through the atmospheric cellars before tastings. An educational, intimate experience focused on world-class sparkling wines. Sophisticated and historic with a sense of discovery.
policyNotes: Appointment only for all tours and tastings.
Unable to accommodate pets. Only service animals permitted. Also cannot accommodate babies or children.

wineries.name: V. Sattui Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A beloved Napa destination known for its incredible artisan deli, 300 cheese varieties, and 2+...
wineries.editorial: A beloved Napa destination known for its incredible artisan deli, 300 cheese varieties, and 2+ acres of shaded picnic grounds under giant oak trees. Perfect for a leisurely afternoon with wine, gourmet food, and outdoor relaxation. Weekend food trucks serve BBQ favorites. Casual, fun, and perfect for groups and families. A complete wine country experience.
policyNotes: Reservations highly recommended for weekends due to limited capacity. Walk-ins welcome based on availability.
Dogs welcome in outdoor picnic spaces if leashed and well-behaved. Not allowed in tasting rooms.

wineries.name: Beringer Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Napa Valley's oldest continuously operating winery featuring the stunning 1884 Rhine House - a 17-room...
wineries.editorial: Napa Valley's oldest continuously operating winery featuring the stunning 1884 Rhine House - a 17-room Victorian mansion built as a replica of the founder's German childhood home. Tours through historic wine caves and tastings on the sprawling veranda transport visitors to another era. Classic, historic, and quintessentially Napa with genuine dog-friendly hospitality.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended. Plan ahead rather than walking in.
Dogs genuinely welcome. All ages and four-legged friends welcome at certain experiences.

wineries.name: Far Niente Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The name means 'without a care' in Italian, and the experience embodies that philosophy.
wineries.editorial: The name means 'without a care' in Italian, and the experience embodies that philosophy. A hidden gem set on 13 acres of exquisitely landscaped gardens with southern-style azalea plantings. The 19th-century stone winery and magical wine caves create an atmosphere that is elegant, relaxing, and truly memorable. Ultra-premium and intimate.
policyNotes: Appointment only. Book through Tock or by phone.
Pets not permitted on tours and tastings.

wineries.name: Buena Vista Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: California's first premium winery (founded 1857) with historic caves and a French countryside ambiance...
wineries.editorial: California's first premium winery (founded 1857) with historic caves and a French countryside ambiance. Features the original 1862 Press House tasting room, hand-dug caves from the 1850s, and a glamorous Bubble Lounge. Winner of 2024 Sonoma Valley People's Choice Best Winery award.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended, especially for seated tastings. Walk-ins welcome at the bar.
Dogs allowed, must be on leash at all times

wineries.name: Gundlach Bundschu Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Laid-back, fun, family-run winery producing wines since 1858.
wineries.editorial: Laid-back, fun, family-run winery producing wines since 1858. Features outdoor tasting on the banks of a scenic pond at the foot of Sonoma Hills with olive groves, wooded hillside trails, and rustic picnic tables under oak trees. Known for witty, relaxed staff and a welcoming atmosphere for families and dogs.
policyNotes: Reservations encouraged, especially weekends. Walk-ins more likely accommodated on weekdays.
Leashed dogs welcome throughout the grounds

wineries.name: Matanzas Creek Winery
wineries.address: 6097 Bennett Valley Rd, Santa Rosa, CA 95404
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A serene paradise featuring famous lavender fields (peak bloom mid-June through July), majestic ancient oaks,...
wineries.editorial: A serene paradise featuring famous lavender fields (peak bloom mid-June through July), majestic ancient oaks, and aromatic wines. Offers a peaceful escape with bocce ball courts, picnic areas, and stunning garden views. Located in beautiful Bennett Valley, just 15 minutes from downtown Santa Rosa.
policyNotes: Reservations requested but walk-ins accommodated on first-come, first-served basis.
Pets welcome on grounds (leashed), but not allowed during seated tasting experiences

wineries.name: St. Francis Winery & Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Renowned for its exceptional five-course wine and food pairings in an elegant estate dining room...
wineries.editorial: Renowned for its exceptional five-course wine and food pairings in an elegant estate dining room with stunning vineyard views. Features Executive Chef-prepared seasonal dishes paired with award-winning wines. A sophisticated culinary destination that's been perfecting wine country cuisine for over 55 years.
policyNotes: Reservations highly recommended for seamless experience. Walk-ins welcome if space available.
Dog-friendly winery, pets welcome

wineries.name: Ferrari-Carano Vineyards & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An opulent estate embodying 'La Bella Vita' (the good life) with the grand Villa Fiore...
wineries.editorial: An opulent estate embodying 'La Bella Vita' (the good life) with the grand Villa Fiore hospitality center surrounded by exquisite gardens, fountains, and 100-year-old olive trees. Features meticulously maintained grounds rivaling the finest estates in wine country. Located in picturesque Dry Creek Valley with breathtaking vineyard views.
policyNotes: Open by appointment only. Groups of 8+ require advance group reservations via events@ffws.com
Unable to accommodate pets

wineries.name: Jordan Vineyard & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An iconic French chateau-inspired 1,200-acre estate offering luxury wine country experiences.
wineries.editorial: An iconic French chateau-inspired 1,200-acre estate offering luxury wine country experiences. Features ivy-covered brick walls, rolling vineyard views, and exclusive tours via Mercedes Sprinter through pristine natural habitats and olive groves. Over three-quarters of the land is dedicated to natural preservation. The epitome of elegant, upscale Sonoma wine tasting.
policyNotes: Advance reservations required for all experiences. Book online or call. Online reservations must be made 4+ hours ahead due to culinary preparations.
Service animals only

wineries.name: Francis Ford Coppola Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A one-of-a-kind wine country destination combining wine, food, film, and fun.
wineries.editorial: A one-of-a-kind wine country destination combining wine, food, film, and fun. Features iconic movie memorabilia from The Godfather and Apocalypse Now, including Oscar statuettes. Unique amenities include a swimming pool with private cabines, bocce courts, and full restaurant. Winner of 2024 Press Democrat Best Winery, Best Bocce, and Best Winery to Take Visitors awards.
policyNotes: Reservations available for private experiences and cabines. Walk-ins welcome for basic tastings.
Service dogs only. Puppies and dogs-in-training also permitted.

wineries.name: Kunde Family Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A casual, laid-back family estate featuring half a mile of wine-aging caves tunneled through 5-million-year-old...
wineries.editorial: A casual, laid-back family estate featuring half a mile of wine-aging caves tunneled through 5-million-year-old volcanic lava flows. Offers diverse experiences from patio sipping by the pond to mountaintop tastings at 1,400-foot elevation with panoramic Sonoma Valley views. Known for approachable prices and beautiful vineyard scenery.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended for Kinneybrook Room and cave tour experiences. Book for parties of 2-10.
Well-behaved leashed dogs welcome (one per reservation) in Kinneybrook Room tastings. No pets on cave tours.

wineries.name: Ravenswood Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: IMPORTANT: Multiple sources indicate Ravenswood Winery's tasting room may be permanently closed.
wineries.editorial: IMPORTANT: Multiple sources indicate Ravenswood Winery's tasting room may be permanently closed. Known historically for their 'No Wimpy Wines' motto and legendary Zinfandels. Please contact directly to verify current operating status before planning a visit.
policyNotes: Tours at 10:30am; groups of 8+ require prior reservations. NOTE: Winery may be permanently closed - please call to verify.
Unable to verify due to reported closure

wineries.name: Gloria Ferrer Caves & Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: California's most awarded sparkling winery, established in 1986 in the rolling Carneros hills.
wineries.editorial: California's most awarded sparkling winery, established in 1986 in the rolling Carneros hills. Features spectacular Vista Terrace views overlooking estate vineyards and culinary experiences pairing sparkling wines with seasonal small bites. Spanish heritage with a sophisticated, celebratory atmosphere perfect for special occasions.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended, especially on weekends. Walk-ins welcome Monday-Thursday. Book via phone or email reservations@gloriaferrer.com
Pets not permitted except service animals

wineries.name: Benziger Family Winery
wineries.address: 1883 London Ranch Rd, Glen Ellen, CA 95442
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A biodynamic estate nestled in an inactive volcanic caldera with postcard-perfect scenery including ponds, redwood...
wineries.editorial: A biodynamic estate nestled in an inactive volcanic caldera with postcard-perfect scenery including ponds, redwood forests, and wildlife around every corner. The award-winning tram tour educates visitors about sustainable farming while winding through vineyards and gardens. Features sheep that help cultivate the landscape, creating a magical, eco-conscious wine experience.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended for tram tours. Contact via phone or email guestservices@benziger.com
Leashed dogs allowed in tasting room and outdoor areas

wineries.name: Dry Creek Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: One of California's last truly family-owned wineries offering a relaxed outdoor wine country experience...
wineries.editorial: One of California's last truly family-owned wineries offering a relaxed outdoor wine country experience. Features beautiful picnic grounds, bocce ball courts, and stunning vineyard views. Known for varietal-defining wines and a peaceful setting where you can spend a leisurely afternoon with a picnic lunch and award-winning wines.
policyNotes: Reservations strongly encouraged. Same-day reservations: call (707) 433-1000 ext. 106. Walk-ins welcomed.
Leashed pets welcome in spacious outdoor seating area with vineyard views

wineries.name: Chalk Hill Estate Vineyards & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An expansive 1,300-acre bucolic estate featuring hillside vineyards, organic culinary gardens, and grand light-filled buildings...
wineries.editorial: An expansive 1,300-acre bucolic estate featuring hillside vineyards, organic culinary gardens, and grand light-filled buildings. Offers exceptional culinary experiences with an acclaimed on-site chef, including multi-course lunches paired with small-lot wines. Tours range from 1 to 5 hours, including unique Hummer estate tours through the property.
policyNotes: Reservations encouraged but not required. Refundable up to 48 hours prior; non-refundable within 48 hours.
Dogs welcome in outdoor areas only, must remain leashed. Service dogs only on Culinary Tours.

wineries.name: Rodney Strong Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A sustainability-focused winery known for hosting popular outdoor summer concerts and events.
wineries.editorial: A sustainability-focused winery known for hosting popular outdoor summer concerts and events. Features 11 sustainable-certified estate vineyards and a welcoming terrace and green space perfect for enjoying wines with your dog. Committed to environmental preservation while producing exceptional Sonoma County wines from premier appellations.
policyNotes: Reservations highly recommended. Walk-ins accepted if space available.
Well-behaved leashed dogs welcome on Terrace and Green areas. Not permitted inside Tasting Room or at winery events/concerts.

wineries.name: MacRostie Winery & Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A sleek, contemporary Estate House perched on a picturesque Russian River Valley hilltop, blending modern...
wineries.editorial: A sleek, contemporary Estate House perched on a picturesque Russian River Valley hilltop, blending modern architecture with breathtaking natural views. Features multiple indoor venues and three expansive patio terraces overlooking vineyards. Renowned for exceptional Chardonnays and Pinot Noirs from the Russian River Valley and Sonoma Coast. A sophisticated, design-forward tasting experience.
policyNotes: Reservations required. Book through website or Tock.
Service animals permitted throughout. Other dogs must remain leashed and under owner's control at all times.

wineries.name: Domaine Serene
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Ultra-premium, world-class estate with breathtaking hilltop views.
wineries.editorial: Ultra-premium, world-class estate with breathtaking hilltop views. Feels like stepping into another country - Italian villa atmosphere with limestone tasting rooms and stunning vineyard panoramas. America's Most Awarded Winery with an ethereal, sophisticated ambiance.
policyNotes: Reservations required for all hosted tastings. Groups over 9 must contact event department. Email hospitality@domaineserene.com for parties larger than 8.
Non-service animals allowed on patio during season

wineries.name: Domaine Roy & Fils
wineries.address: 8351 NE Worden Hill Road, Dundee, OR 97115
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Burgundian-influenced estate with panoramic breathtaking views even on cloudy days.
wineries.editorial: Burgundian-influenced estate with panoramic breathtaking views even on cloudy days. Gorgeous tasting room with large windows overlooking a huge patio and vineyards. Mediterranean charcuterie available. Immediately relaxing atmosphere with fabulous indoor and outdoor seating areas.
policyNotes: Book via Tock. Last reservation at 4:00 PM. Indoor and outdoor seating available with heaters and blankets.
Friendly, well-trained dogs welcome on leash on patio only

wineries.name: Sokol Blosser Vineyards
wineries.address: 5000 NE Sokol Blosser Lane, Dayton, OR 97114
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Pioneer family winery blending modern elegance with breathtaking floor-to-ceiling vineyard views.
wineries.editorial: Pioneer family winery blending modern elegance with breathtaking floor-to-ceiling vineyard views. Second-generation winegrowers committed to sustainability - first US winery with LEED certification and a Certified B Corporation. Excellent food options including artisanal popcorn, charcuterie, and entrees. Farm & Forage experiences available.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended especially on weekends. Walk-ins accommodated when possible. Book online or by phone.
Friendly dogs on leashes welcome in outdoor spaces. Service animals welcome inside tasting room.

wineries.name: Stoller Family Estate
wineries.vibeDescriptor: USA Today's #1 rated tasting room in the nation.
wineries.editorial: USA Today's #1 rated tasting room in the nation. World's first LEED Gold certified winery with a net-zero tasting room powered 100% by solar. Panoramic vineyard views, seasonally-rotating wine country cuisine, cheese and charcuterie boards. Very welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere with lawn space for relaxing. EV charging stations available.
policyNotes: Reservations available but walk-ins always welcome. Call for parties of 13 or more.
Dogs on leash welcome on patio and lawn spaces. No pets inside tasting room except service animals.

wineries.name: Domaine Drouhin Oregon
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Authentic French winemaking heritage - owned by the Drouhin Family of Burgundy since 1987.
wineries.editorial: Authentic French winemaking heritage - owned by the Drouhin Family of Burgundy since 1987. Four-level gravity flow winery perched high with wonderful eastern valley views. Laid back, pleasant atmosphere with tastings on expansive terrace or in Secret Garden. Unique experiences comparing Oregon and Burgundy wines. No food available for purchase - intimate, wine-focused experience.
policyNotes: Reservations highly encouraged, walk-ins welcome as space allows. Book up to 90 days in advance. Max 4 people per tasting. Call or text for waitlist.
Dog-friendly in designated outdoor areas

wineries.name: Argyle Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Oregon's premier sparkling wine destination in a modern, sleek, spacious Tasting House.
wineries.editorial: Oregon's premier sparkling wine destination in a modern, sleek, spacious Tasting House. Surrounded by lush Pacific Northwest-inspired gardens with warm, inviting setting. Located conveniently on Highway 99W in downtown Dundee. No vineyard views but beautiful, relaxing, well-designed atmosphere. Food available through Trellis Mobile Wood-Fire Kitchen partnership and vegan/regular charcuterie boxes.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended for seated tasting experience. Walk-ins welcome based on availability.
Well-behaved, leashed dogs welcome on outdoor patio. Service dogs permitted throughout property.

wineries.name: Ponzi Vineyards
wineries.address: 19500 SW Mountain Home Road, Sherwood, OR 97140
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Internationally acclaimed pioneer winery with 50+ years of family winemaking.
wineries.editorial: Internationally acclaimed pioneer winery with 50+ years of family winemaking. Stunning modern tasting room with floor-to-ceiling glass windows offering breathtaking Chehalem Mountains vineyard and valley views. Seasonal culinary menu crafted with local farmers and artisans. Fireside seating, covered terrace, and bocce ball courts. LIVE-certified sustainable and organic farming methods.
policyNotes: Reservations strongly encouraged. Walk-ins welcome as space allows. Email reservations@ponzivineyards.com or call for cancellations.
Well-behaved dogs welcome on lower terrace. Must remain on leash and under physical control.

wineries.name: Erath Winery
wineries.address: 9409 NE Worden Hill Road, Dundee, OR 97115
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Historic pioneer winery founded in 1968 - one of Oregon's original wine estates.
wineries.editorial: Historic pioneer winery founded in 1968 - one of Oregon's original wine estates. Currently operating with limited availability and special curated experiences by appointment. Contact winery directly for current status and booking. Portland Pearl District urban tasting room is currently closed.
policyNotes: Advanced reservations required. Contact winery directly for current availability and special curated experiences.
Contact winery directly to inquire about current dog policy

wineries.name: Willamette Valley Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Scenic, inviting destination with breathtaking views and relaxed atmosphere.
wineries.editorial: Scenic, inviting destination with breathtaking views and relaxed atmosphere. Pacific Northwest-inspired food menu with vegetarian and vegan options. Wine blending experiences available. Extended Friday and Saturday hours until 8 PM. Sustainable practices throughout. Multiple locations including Vancouver Waterfront with Columbia River views.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended for indoor tableside service. Walk-ins welcome for indoor/outdoor open seating with bar-side service.
Dogs welcome on Pinot Decks and adjacent lawns. No pets in tasting room except service animals.

wineries.name: King Estate Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Largest Biodynamic certified vineyard in North America with 1,033 acres of certified organic vineyards...
wineries.editorial: Largest Biodynamic certified vineyard in North America with 1,033 acres of certified organic vineyards. Tasting room atop vineyard with stunning valley views - outdoor patio not to be missed. 30 acres of organic fruits, vegetables, and flowers. Complimentary tastings of Signature Pinot Gris, Rose, and Pinot Noir available. Note: Historic restaurant has closed and is transitioning to new concept.
policyNotes: Reservations required. Tastings are up to 2 hours.
No pets allowed indoors or outdoors

wineries.name: Adelsheim Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Seven-time Wine & Spirits Top 100 Winery with LIVE certified sustainable vineyards.
wineries.editorial: Seven-time Wine & Spirits Top 100 Winery with LIVE certified sustainable vineyards. Gorgeous covered patio and lush gardens overlooking vineyards with comfortable chairs and sofas. Trek & Taste experiences through the estate with fresh berries and ingredients from Jack's Garden. Peaceful, refined atmosphere perfect for lingering.
policyNotes: Reservations required. Book in advance to secure tasting time slot.
Contact winery directly to inquire about dog policy

wineries.name: Chehalem Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Estate tasting room with stunning views of Parrett Mountain and Mount Hood to the east.
wineries.editorial: Estate tasting room with stunning views of Parrett Mountain and Mount Hood to the east. Full kitchen with chef-prepared food including summer grilled menu on Pinot Patio. Thoughtful, tasteful atmosphere with friendly, knowledgeable staff. Private tastings paired with cheese and charcuterie. Two convenient locations - estate in Sherwood and downtown Newberg.
policyNotes: Reservations available but walk-ins always welcome. Private tastings and tours available for $50/person.
Well-behaved dogs welcome outside on leash

wineries.name: Elk Cove Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family-owned estate tucked into Coast Range foothills with what Robert Parker called the best view...
wineries.editorial: Family-owned estate tucked into Coast Range foothills with what Robert Parker called the best view of all Oregon wineries. Spectacular vineyard and mountain panoramas from spacious patio and tasting room. Flights & Bites events with food pairings. High-volume tourist attraction but maintains quality service. Excellent value with affordable tasting fees.
policyNotes: Seated tastings require 24-hour advance reservation. Walk-ins welcome for outdoor area but tables fill up fast.
Dog-friendly vineyard

wineries.name: Penner-Ash Wine Cellars
wineries.address: 15771 NE Ribbon Ridge Road, Newberg, OR 97132
wineries.vibeDescriptor: LIVE Certified sustainable gravity-flow winery with inspiring hilltop views including Mount Hood vistas...
wineries.editorial: LIVE Certified sustainable gravity-flow winery with inspiring hilltop views including Mount Hood vistas. Warm, casual, family-friendly atmosphere with welcoming staff. Legacy Tasting features library wines paired with locally sourced seasonal bites. Cellar Club members get exclusive patio access with bottle service and spectacular views. Top-notch food and wine pairings.
policyNotes: Walk-in guests warmly welcomed on first-come, first-served basis. Reservations also available.
Dogs are part of the Penner-Ash family. Furry companions must remain on leash in outdoor spaces like the patio.

wineries.name: Cristom Vineyards
wineries.address: 6905 Spring Valley Road NW, Salem, OR 97304
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 240-acre estate nestled in volcanic Eola-Amity hillside with picturesque vineyard overlook views.
wineries.editorial: 240-acre estate nestled in volcanic Eola-Amity hillside with picturesque vineyard overlook views. Biodynamic and organic farming for purest terroir expression. Winemaker experience includes artisanal charcuterie pairings. Immersion experiences include strolls through seasonal food gardens. Whole-cluster fermentation and low-intervention winemaking philosophy. Dogs get estate water and treats - truly welcoming atmosphere.
policyNotes: Text or call (503) 375-3068 or email hospitality@cristomvineyards.com to make reservations.
Dogs on leashes welcome in outside areas only. Estate water and pup treats available.

wineries.name: L'Ecole No 41
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A charming, historic experience housed in a beautifully restored 1915 schoolhouse.
wineries.editorial: A charming, historic experience housed in a beautifully restored 1915 schoolhouse. The atmosphere blends old-world character with refined wine country hospitality. Enjoy tastings in the original classrooms or on the scenic outdoor deck overlooking wheat fields and vineyards.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome; reservations recommended for groups
Dogs welcome on grounds, lawn, and deck; not allowed inside tasting room

wineries.name: Seven Hills Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An elegant, refined tasting room in downtown Walla Walla's historic Whitehouse-Crawford building, originally a 1904...
wineries.editorial: An elegant, refined tasting room in downtown Walla Walla's historic Whitehouse-Crawford building, originally a 1904 wood mill. The space is polished and Instagram-worthy with gorgeous tables and attentive staff. A sophisticated urban wine experience with a working winery feel.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome; reservations recommended; required for groups of 7+
Service animals only (call ahead to confirm current policy)

wineries.name: Doubleback Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An exclusive, appointment-only estate winery founded by NFL legend Drew Bledsoe.
wineries.editorial: An exclusive, appointment-only estate winery founded by NFL legend Drew Bledsoe. The focus is on world-class Cabernet Sauvignon from estate vineyards. The experience feels private and prestigious, catering primarily to mailing list members seeking premium, allocated wines.
policyNotes: Appointment required; primarily for mailing list members
Contact winery for current policy

wineries.name: Leonetti Cellar
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The original Walla Walla cult winery and a true legend.
wineries.editorial: The original Walla Walla cult winery and a true legend. Leonetti does not offer public tastings - wines are available exclusively through their coveted mailing list with a 3-4 year waiting list. Members receive one annual visit opportunity during Spring Release Weekend. This is Washington wine royalty.
policyNotes: No public tastings; mailing list members only (Spring Release Weekend in May)
Not applicable (no public visits)

wineries.name: Pepper Bridge Winery

policyNotes: Reservations recommended; walk-ins welcome as space allows
Dog friendly

The industrial-chic space features art displays and a welcoming courtyard where dogs are welcome. Known for friendly hospitality and their resident winery dog greeting guests.

Dog friendly in outdoor courtyard; winery dog often greets guests

wineries.name: Gramercy Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A sommelier's dream winery founded by Master Sommelier Greg Harrington.
wineries.editorial: A sommelier's dream winery founded by Master Sommelier Greg Harrington. The focus is on Rhone and Bordeaux-style wines crafted with 'a sommelier's palate, a farmer's thumb, and a winemaker's soul.' Sophisticated yet unpretentious, this is a destination for serious wine enthusiasts seeking exceptional, terroir-driven wines.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended; walk-ins welcome as space allows
Contact winery for current policy

wineries.name: Saviah Cellars

wineries.vibeDescriptor: A welcoming, laid-back winery in the Southside district with generous outdoor space including a patio...
wineries.editorial: A welcoming, laid-back winery in the Southside district with generous outdoor space including a patio and lawn. Very dog-friendly with treats on hand for four-legged visitors. The atmosphere is relaxed and unpretentious - bring your own picnic to enjoy outside while sipping excellent wines.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended; walk-ins welcome based on availability; groups of 6+ must email in advance
Dog friendly outdoors; dogs welcome on patio and lawn with leash; treats available

wineries.name: Amavi Cellars
wineries.address: 3796 Peppers Bridge Road, Walla Walla, WA 99362
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A beautiful Southside winery with sweeping views of Pepper Bridge Estate Vineyard and the Blue...
wineries.editorial: A beautiful Southside winery with sweeping views of Pepper Bridge Estate Vineyard and the Blue Mountains. Multiple outdoor decks offer dog-friendly spaces with water bowls and treats. Committed to sustainability - 100% estate, 100% certified sustainable. A welcoming, view-focused experience that feels both refined and approachable.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome; reservations available to secure specific dates/experiences
Dogs welcome on North Deck and Lower Level Patio; water bowls and treats provided; must be leashed

wineries.name: Foundry Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A unique fusion of art and wine in a converted historic machine shop.
wineries.editorial: A unique fusion of art and wine in a converted historic machine shop. Features a contemporary art gallery, outdoor sculpture garden, and curated design shop with handcrafted gifts from 100+ independent artists. Organic, low-intervention wines pair with a creative, gallery-like atmosphere. Perfect for art lovers and wine enthusiasts alike.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome; private tastings available by appointment
Dogs welcome in Sculpture Garden (leashed); not inside gallery

wineries.name: Chateau Ste. Michelle
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Washington's grand dame of wine on a stunning 118-acre estate with manicured grounds, historic chateau...
wineries.editorial: Washington's grand dame of wine on a stunning 118-acre estate with manicured grounds, historic chateau architecture, and famous summer concert series. A quintessential wine country destination that feels like a European estate. Perfect for picnics, special events, and introducing newcomers to Washington wine. Casual elegance with broad appeal.
policyNotes: Walk-ins and reservations available; first come, first serve for some experiences
Dogs welcome on outdoor patio (leashed); not allowed inside or during concerts; water bowls and treats available

wineries.name: DeLille Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An upscale Woodinville destination in the Old Redhook Brewery complex featuring both a tasting room...
wineries.editorial: An upscale Woodinville destination in the Old Redhook Brewery complex featuring both a tasting room and full-service restaurant. Known for exceptional Bordeaux-style blends. The atmosphere is polished and elevated, perfect for a special occasion or pairing wine with fine dining. The seasonal outdoor deck adds a relaxed element.
policyNotes: Reservations encouraged; walk-ins accommodated as space allows; 24-hour cancellation requested
Dogs allowed on first-floor patio and The Deck (seasonal); not inside due to health regulations

wineries.name: Matthews Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A charming farm-style winery with a welcoming lawn and covered patio.
wineries.editorial: A charming farm-style winery with a welcoming lawn and covered patio. The vibe is relaxed and family-friendly, perfect for lounging outdoors with a bottle of wine and your dog. No pretense here - just good wine in a casual, comfortable setting with plenty of outdoor space to spread out.
policyNotes: Reservations available; lawn open for glass/bottle purchases without reservation
Dogs welcome on covered patio and upper lawn (leashed); not allowed inside

wineries.name: Mark Ryan Winery
wineries.address: 14200 NE 145th Street, Suite D, Woodinville, WA 98072
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A rock and roll winery with serious attitude.
wineries.editorial: A rock and roll winery with serious attitude. The open, modern tasting room features vintage rock and roll decor including a vintage Indian motorcycle in the lobby. Bold red wines match the edgy vibe. The upstairs outdoor balcony is perfect for dogs and people-watching. Unapologetically cool without being exclusive.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome; reservations optional with $35 deposit (refundable with bottle purchase)
Dogs welcome on patio and covered outdoor deck; water bowls and treats available; not inside due to food program

wineries.name: Januik Winery (Novelty Hill-Januik)
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A sleek, modern winery with stunning contemporary architecture that Wine Spectator called 'architecturally stunning...
wineries.editorial: A sleek, modern winery with stunning contemporary architecture that Wine Spectator called 'architecturally stunning.' Two independent wineries (Novelty Hill and Januik) share this state-of-the-art facility under acclaimed winemaker Mike Januik. The expansive gardens and patio create an elegant outdoor experience. Sophisticated and photo-worthy.
policyNotes: No appointment needed for groups of 7 or less; required for groups of 8+
Dogs welcome in outdoor patio area; service animals only inside

wineries.name: Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Historic and prestigious winery with scenic Keuka Lake views, offering an elegant yet welcoming atmosphere...
wineries.editorial: Historic and prestigious winery with scenic Keuka Lake views, offering an elegant yet welcoming atmosphere. Known as the pioneer of vinifera grapes in the Finger Lakes, the tasting room features knowledgeable, friendly staff and offers everything from complimentary tastings to the upscale 1886 Reserve Room experience with food pairings. Educational and refined but not stuffy.
policyNotes: Reservations required for groups of 12+ ($5/person non-refundable fee). Reservations recommended for premium experiences.
Dogs welcome on outdoor lawn areas. Service animals always permitted per ADA.

wineries.name: Red Tail Ridge Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Modern, clean, and eco-conscious with an elegant-industrial aesthetic.
wineries.editorial: Modern, clean, and eco-conscious with an elegant-industrial aesthetic. New York's first LEED Gold Certified winery featuring geothermal heating/cooling and sustainable practices. Beautiful contemporary tasting room with natural light and stunning woodwork. Exceptionally dog-friendly with dedicated spaces for pet owners.
policyNotes: Reservations required for some experiences. Dog-friendly tastings available by reservation.
Dog-friendly tasting room - leashed dogs welcome inside. Special Dog Friendly Tasting reservations available in dedicated space.

wineries.name: Heron Hill Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Breathtaking and architecturally stunning.
wineries.editorial: Breathtaking and architecturally stunning. Rated one of the most spectacular tasting rooms in the world by Travel + Leisure, the Greek Revival building features a silo-like tower, soaring arched ceilings designed to evoke a wine barrel, and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Keuka Lake. The atmosphere is easy-going despite the elegant surroundings, with knowledgeable staff.
policyNotes: Reservations available online. Large groups should call ahead.
Pet friendly winery

wineries.name: Hermann J. Wiemer Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Prestigious and celebrated, with a tasting room adjacent to production areas allowing guests to watch...
wineries.editorial: Prestigious and celebrated, with a tasting room adjacent to production areas allowing guests to watch winemaking in action. Staff are friendly and eager to share the vineyard's history. Can get busy with wine enthusiasts. One of America's most acclaimed Riesling producers, having received Wine & Spirits Top 100 Wineries award twelve times. Sophisticated but welcoming.
policyNotes: Reservations recommended for guided tastings. Walk-ins welcome as space allows. Book via Tock.
Pets welcome; must remain leashed and with owner at all times. Dogs allowed inside and out with reservation.

wineries.name: Ravines Wine Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: High-end yet rustic atmosphere housed in a beautiful historic barn with high wooden beams and...
wineries.editorial: High-end yet rustic atmosphere housed in a beautiful historic barn with high wooden beams and slate roof at the Geneva location. The Keuka tasting room offers gorgeous lake views from a large patio. Widely recognized as one of the best wineries in the Finger Lakes, offering refined tastings with seasonal food pairings. Donkeys on the property add charm for families.
policyNotes: Reservations strongly encouraged. Maximum 6 people per general tasting reservation.
Dogs welcome at outdoor patio seating at Geneva location. Donkeys on property fun for kids.

wineries.name: Wagner Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Warm and inviting destination winery with stunning Seneca Lake views.
wineries.editorial: Warm and inviting destination winery with stunning Seneca Lake views. Features the Ginny Lee Cafe with cathedral ceilings, massive windows, and outdoor patio seating overlooking vineyards and lake. Also houses Wagner Valley Brewing Co. craft brewery. Relaxed, all-day destination atmosphere perfect for lunch and leisurely tastings.
policyNotes: Online booking available. Reservations recommended for groups.
Due to Food Modernization Act, only service animals inside (open production areas). Leashed dogs welcome on the lawn.

wineries.name: Anthony Road Wine Company
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Relaxed, friendly atmosphere with excellent wines in an open, airy tasting room.
wineries.editorial: Relaxed, friendly atmosphere with excellent wines in an open, airy tasting room. Features beautiful charming gardens and spectacular Seneca Lake views from the patio. Seated tastings by appointment create an intimate experience. The gardens are absolutely stunning and visitors can enjoy a glass or bottle outside with friends while taking in the scenery.
policyNotes: Reservations strongly encouraged. Maximum group size of 6 people, no exceptions or splitting groups.
Leashed, well-behaved pets permitted at outside tables only.

wineries.name: Fox Run Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Upbeat, welcoming, and refreshingly unpretentious with 'no velvet ropes, no stuffy tastings, no exclusivity contests...
wineries.editorial: Upbeat, welcoming, and refreshingly unpretentious with 'no velvet ropes, no stuffy tastings, no exclusivity contests.' Beautiful Seneca Lake setting with fantastic ambiance. The fully house-made cafe features local ingredients and dishes like bison tacos. Excellent value tastings with friendly, knowledgeable hosts. Dog-friendly and family-welcoming atmosphere.
policyNotes: Reservations only required for groups of 13+ for wine tastings. Tour tickets purchased in tasting room.
Friendly, leashed dogs welcome at main Tasting Room bar and back patio/yard. Not allowed in Cafe area or front deck due to health codes.

wineries.name: Lakewood Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Casual, fun, warm, and inviting - everyone's there to have a good time, taste wine,...
wineries.editorial: Casual, fun, warm, and inviting - everyone's there to have a good time, taste wine, and have a few laughs. Owner Chris Stamp often provides wine explanations with a clever sense of humor. Exceptionally dog-friendly with resident dog Fizzy. Spectacular Seneca Lake views and charming outdoor tasting area with cozy heaters for cooler months. Family-welcoming with expansive grounds.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome. Check website for tour availability.
Dog-loving, dog-friendly winery! Dogs welcome. You'll likely meet their resident dog Fizzy.

wineries.name: Lamoreaux Landing Wine Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Sleek, modern, and elegant Greek Revival building with soaring high ceilings, light wood throughout, and...
wineries.editorial: Sleek, modern, and elegant Greek Revival building with soaring high ceilings, light wood throughout, and floor-to-ceiling windows offering unparalleled 25+ mile views of Seneca Lake. Social and active atmosphere with everyone enjoying being there. Features a glass-walled private room with indoor citrus trees. More formal but very welcoming, with wine-and-cheese pairings and chocolate flights available.
policyNotes: Reservations highly encouraged (cannot guarantee table without). Maximum table size of 8. Last reservation for tables of 8 at 3:30 PM.
Leashed, well-behaved dogs welcome in outdoor areas and tasting room.

wineries.name: Paumanok Vineyards
wineries.address: 1074 Main Road (Route 25), P.O. Box 741, Aquebogue, NY 11931
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Peaceful, relaxed family-owned vineyard set back from the road for a tranquil experience.
wineries.editorial: Peaceful, relaxed family-owned vineyard set back from the road for a tranquil experience. Beautiful back deck with large wooden tables and Adirondack chairs on the lawn among vines. BYO food encouraged for picnics. Each family member makes guests feel part of the family. Has received Governor's Cup and Winery of the Year, and been featured in White House wine service. One of the best on the North Fork.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome for groups of 7 or less. Prepaid reservations accepted. Groups larger than 7: email res@paumanok.com
Pets welcome Monday through Friday only. No pets on Saturdays and Sundays.

wineries.name: Macari Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Warm, welcoming atmosphere with spectacular vineyard views from the airy tasting room, grand fireplace, and...
wineries.editorial: Warm, welcoming atmosphere with spectacular vineyard views from the airy tasting room, grand fireplace, and beautiful stone and timber deck. Leader in sustainable and biodynamic viticulture for 30+ years with cattle for composting and no herbicides. Meadowlark's Wine Bar offers thoughtfully curated pours. First-come, first-served lawn seating among the vines. Voted Best Vineyard on Long Island 2025.
policyNotes: Reservations required for all tastings. Email reservations@macariwines.com
Dogs welcome on lawn area among vines, must be leashed. Not permitted indoors or on covered deck due to health regulations.

wineries.name: Bedell Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: California wine experience vibe in a renovated potato barn.
wineries.editorial: California wine experience vibe in a renovated potato barn. Steel bar and black accents create modern juxtaposition with the historic structure, while modern art from NYC commissioned artists dots the walls. Massive, airy space with clean farmhouse aesthetic. Vast outdoor seating overlooks vineyards with seasonal live music (blues bands). Contemporary but accessible, feeling transported to a metropolitan frame of mind.
policyNotes: Walk-ins welcome. Reservations recommended for parties of 6 or more.
Dogs welcome, should be leashed and mindful of other guests.

wineries.name: Wolffer Estate Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Where Long Island countryside meets Hamptons sophistication.
wineries.editorial: Where Long Island countryside meets Hamptons sophistication. Iconic, sexy, world-renowned destination with a bright tasting room where locals and city escapees gather over flights of crisp rose. Upscale yet not overly pretentious, ideal for wine enthusiasts and families alike. Summer evenings feature tastings, open-air gatherings, live music, and sunset watching beneath the pergola. Weathered leather couches inside, manicured vineyards beyond the patio.
policyNotes: Reservation only for seated experiences featuring wines, small bites, and charcuterie.
Animals not permitted. Only ADA service animals (including psychiatric service dogs) accommodated.

wineries.name: Sparkling Pointe
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Vibrant but laid-back elegance in a gorgeous, spacious facility with tall ceilings, huge windows, and...
wineries.editorial: Vibrant but laid-back elegance in a gorgeous, spacious facility with tall ceilings, huge windows, and ornate chandeliers. Modern white and gray palette with splashes of Brazilian Carnaval-inspired color in the art. Solely produces sparkling wines via methode champenoise with surprising variety. Large outdoor terrace overlooks vineyards with great sunset views. More expensive than typical wineries but delivers a premium champagne-house experience.
policyNotes: Reservations accepted for seated wine service. Walk-ins and day-of reservations welcome. Groups of 6 or less for general reservations.
Only ADA Service Animals permitted. Comfort/emotional support animals do not qualify and are not permitted.

wineries.name: Slater Run Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A quiet, unpretentious hidden gem in Hunt Country with sweeping vineyard views.
wineries.editorial: A quiet, unpretentious hidden gem in Hunt Country. Bright and airy tasting room with rolling hill views. Known by locals while nearby wineries are crowded with tourists. Award-winning wines including white, amber, rose, sparkling, and red varietals. Curated cheese and charcuterie boards available.

Adults only (21+)

wineries.name: Crimson Lane Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Sophisticated elevated wine experience with spectacular Blue Ridge Mountain views.
wineries.editorial: A sophisticated, elevated wine experience with stunning mountain vistas. Napa-designed architecture by Backen & Backen - the first East Coast building by the famed firm.
